path_decisions.rationale: Pheromone confirms this is the highest-weight edge (0.113). Unweighted vote in consolidate_signals is the core issue — it cancels strong convictions
Per-strategy risk budgets prevent correlated drawdowns from blocking uncorrelated strategies — direct win-rate maintainer during one-strategy drawdowns
RiskEngine VaR check (cvar_95 < -0.05) uses hardcoded threshold — may need per-strategy VaR limits. Also, position_limit_pct blocks additional entries when one strategy fills the limit
All signal chain improvements must be validated. The key insight: signal_quality.py already computes hit_rate (precision) per strategy — this should be the win_rate KPI, not backtest win_rate

candidate_solution.summary: Signal pipeline architecture changes: (1) strength-weighted consolidation, (2) per-strategy risk budgets, (3) hit_rate as validation KPI, (4) actual win_rate for Kelly

change_1.title: Replace net-vote with strength-weighted directional consolidation
change_1.current: Net vote: long_signals +1, short_signals -1. When net=0, returns None (FLAT). Two weak signals (0.3 each) can cancel one strong signal (0.8).
change_1.proposed: Weighted consolidation: net_strength = sum(s.direction.value * s.strength for s in signals). direction = sign(net_strength). consolidated.strength = abs(net_strength) / sum(s.strength for s in signals). Add min_consolidation_strength threshold (default=0.3) — discard signals below this. This ensures a strong 0.8 LONG from trend_following is not canceled by a weak 0.4 SHORT from mean_reversion. The stronger conviction wins.
change_1.rationale: Current unweighted vote loses high-conviction signals. When trend_following (win_rate ~0.55) produces a 0.8 strength LONG and mean_reversion (win_rate ~0.48) produces a 0.4 strength SHORT, they cancel. Weighted consolidation lets the higher-performing strategy's conviction through. This directly increases win_rate because higher-confidence signals have higher hit rates (signal_quality.py proves precision correlates with signal conviction).

change_2.title: Add per-strategy risk budget to prevent cross-strategy drawdown blocking
change_2.current: Portfolio-level risk checks only: one strategy's drawdown blocks ALL other strategies from entering new positions.
change_2.proposed: Add strategy_risk_budgets dict to RiskConfig: {strategy_id: {daily_loss_limit, weekly_loss_limit, max_position_pct}}. In RiskEngine.check(), first check per-strategy budget (has this strategy hit its daily/weekly loss limit?), then check portfolio-level limits. If a strategy is at its budget limit, block that strategy's signals but not other strategies'. Only block all strategies at portfolio level (total drawdown > max_drawdown).
change_2.rationale: Multi-strategy systems maintain higher win_rate than single strategies because uncorrelated strategies compensate during drawdowns. But the current portfolio-level risk blocking eliminates this benefit — one strategy's drawdown kills all entries. Per-strategy budgets preserve the diversification benefit, keeping uncorrelated strategies active during correlated drawdowns.

change_3.title: Add per-strategy VaR threshold instead of blanket -0.05 CVaR limit
change_3.current: Single hardcoded cvar_95 < -0.05 threshold blocks all signals. Mean-reversion strategies naturally have higher VaR because they trade against the trend.
change_3.proposed: Add strategy_var_limits dict: {strategy_id: {cvar_threshold}}. Default remains -0.05. For mean_reversion strategies, set cvar_threshold=-0.08 (wider) because MR strategies have fatter left tails by design. For trend_following, keep -0.05. Check signal.strategy_id against strategy_var_limits before VaR check.
change_3.rationale: Mean-reversion strategies have asymmetric return distributions (many small wins, occasional large losses). The blanket -0.05 CVaR threshold was designed for trend-following. It may block valid MR entries during volatile periods when MR opportunities are richest, reducing MR win_rate.

change_4.title: Add hit_rate (signal precision) as primary win_rate KPI alongside backtest win_rate
change_4.current: signal_quality_metrics computes hit_rate (= precision) but it's only used internally in CPCV validation, not as a standalone KPI or optimization objective.
change_4.proposed: Expose hit_rate as 'win_rate' objective option in optimizer.py (_objective_value). Add signal_quality_metrics call to BacktestEngine.run_backtest output. When objective='win_rate', the optimizer and validation gate should use BacktestResult.win_rate (percentage of profitable trades), not signal hit_rate. But signal hit_rate should be a secondary metric reported alongside for diagnostics.
change_4.rationale: Two different 'win rate' concepts: (1) trade win_rate = % of closed trades that are profitable, (2) signal hit_rate = % of entry signals followed by positive next-bar return. Both are useful. Trade win_rate is what the user sees and optimizes. Signal hit_rate validates entry quality. The optimizer should target trade win_rate. The signal_quality module should track hit_rate for diagnostics.

notes: The signal pipeline architecture has two fundamental flaws: (1) unweighted vote that discards strong convictions, and (2) portfolio-level risk blocking that defeats multi-strategy diversification. Both are architectural decisions that were reasonable for a single-strategy system but become anti-patterns in a multi-strategy portfolio. Fixing both simultaneously would compound the win_rate improvement because better signals flow through AND the risk engine doesn't block them unnecessarily.
